Fit & Silhouette.name: Classic Churidar
Fit & Silhouette.description: The original tight-fitting bottom cut on the bias with extra length so the fabric gathers into soft bangle-like folds (churis) around the ankle. Worn under kurtas, Anarkalis, and short kameez.
Fit & Silhouette.notes: The bias-cut construction is what allows the fabric to gather rather than bunch awkwardly at the ankle.

Fit & Silhouette.name: Straight-Fit Churidar
Fit & Silhouette.description: A more relaxed, less body-hugging version of the churidar that skips the extreme ankle gathering for a straighter, easier fit while still tapering slightly at the bottom.
Fit & Silhouette.notes: A common choice for everyday and workplace wear where the traditional snug fit isn't necessary.

Fit & Silhouette.name: Ankle-Length Churidar
Fit & Silhouette.description: Cut to end precisely at the ankle without the extra length needed for bangle folds, giving a cleaner, more modern silhouette closer to a fitted trouser.
Fit & Silhouette.notes: Popular in contemporary Indo-Western styling paired with short kurtis and tunics.

Fabric & Construction.name: Cotton Churidar
Fabric & Construction.description: Made from breathable cotton, the most common and practical churidar fabric for everyday wear, especially in warmer climates.
Fabric & Construction.notes: The default choice for daily wear due to comfort and washability.

Fabric & Construction.name: Silk Churidar
Fabric & Construction.description: Cut from silk or silk-blend fabric to match festive kameez and Anarkali tops, offering a sheen and drape more suited to special occasions than daily cotton churidars.
Fabric & Construction.notes: Usually stitched as part of a matching festive suit set rather than sold standalone.

Fabric & Construction.name: Stretch/Lycra Churidar
Fabric & Construction.description: Blended with lycra or spandex for added stretch, allowing the tight ankle fit to be achieved without the traditional bias-cut tailoring, and making it easier to move in.
Fabric & Construction.notes: Has largely replaced the traditional bias-cut construction in mass-market ready-to-wear churidars.

Fabric & Construction.name: Patiala-Style Churidar Fusion
Fabric & Construction.description: Combines the loose, pleated volume of a Patiala salwar in the upper thigh with a churidar-style gathered taper at the ankle, blending two Punjabi bottom-wear traditions.
Fabric & Construction.notes: A hybrid style that gives the drama of a Patiala salwar with the fitted ankle of a churidar.

Embellishment & Detailing.name: Embroidered Ankle Churidar
Embellishment & Detailing.description: Features chikankari, zari, or thread embroidery concentrated around the ankle opening where the bangle folds gather, adding a decorative detail that shows even under a longer kameez.
Embellishment & Detailing.materials: Cotton or silk, hand or machine embroidery at hem
Embellishment & Detailing.notes: The embroidery is placed specifically to be visible in the folds when the churidar bunches at the ankle.

Embellishment & Detailing.name: Printed Churidar
Embellishment & Detailing.description: Carries block-print, digital print, or ikat-style patterns matching or contrasting with the kameez, offering visual interest without the cost of embroidery.
Embellishment & Detailing.materials: Cotton, block print or digital print
Embellishment & Detailing.notes: A budget-friendly way to coordinate patterns across a two-piece or three-piece suit set.

Embellishment & Detailing.name: Plain/Solid Churidar
Embellishment & Detailing.description: A single solid colour with no embellishment, designed to be paired under heavily worked kurtas or Anarkalis so the bottom stays understated while the top carries the visual detail.
Embellishment & Detailing.notes: The most versatile churidar type, meant to be worn under many different kameez styles.
